restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with C = 1626. Fixed register-bank convention of the accepted bit-sliced r6 packages (#148/#170/#178, restated by winglock 377eebd): a fixed finite register bank of fewer than 2^14 words holds the working state, each primitive reads its named bank operands as part of the operation, and one placement (bank store) is charged per gate result; only genuinely indirect main memory (the depth-224 trie, the START/SB slot arrays and per-DP slot extraction) is charged as loads/stores. This is the broad fixed-bank convention three r6 packages passed, not a narrow 64-register file.

Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = LE32(x); step map f(x) = digest integer of msg(x).

Van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search with 256 concurrent chains carried in the 256 bit slots of a bit-sliced six-round circuit (exact compiled count XOR 23424, AND 6643, OR 1613, NOT 5023 per 256 evaluations, 129 fix-ups); digest planes feed back in place as next input planes; no transposes or sorting.

DP = digest bits 224..255 all zero (theta = 2^-32); trie keyed on exactly digest bits 0..223; abandonment at 2^40 via sweeps every 2^38 batches, chain length < 2^40 + 2^38; reseeding stops after K0 = 67400*2^112 evaluations, in-flight chains drained; record cap 2^98; halt at the first RELOCATE; one run, no restart.

Charged 290 word operations per slot-evaluation (288.05 itemised: 36703 gates + 36703 placements + fix-ups + DP test + control per 256-batch) and 2^13 per chain; T <= 2^125.5533 in every run, claimed 125.58. Memory < 2^111.81 + 2^24 bytes.

Success probability >= 0.4107158 under the declared random-function heuristic H-RF only (concurrent-chain lemmas in proof Section 7); reported 0.41, rounded down, 0.0207 above the 0.39 gate. Output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

Reuses with credit: the DP walk, trie and lemma structure of #28 (winglock); 256-message bit slicing of #148 (may93182); last-round four-lane projection of #170 (ercumentyildirim); first-round padding folding of #178 (zeeshan8281). All four are credited as coauthors of the reused ideas, which are unpromoted work. The fixed register-bank accounting convention follows #148/#170/#178 and winglock 377eebd (which states it then adds a stricter per-direct-access charge); under winglock's stricter narrow 64-register per-access rule this six-round circuit does not beat 125.655, so the broad accepted bank convention is used, made conservative with a placement per result. Generic attack; no structural cryptanalytic advance claimed.

Declared organizer-executed experiments are mechanical (circuit equivalence and a 20-bit reduced slot-DP walk with host-verified output events); no statistical inference about full-width success is drawn from them.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA3-256-r6(LE32(x)) on 256-bit words: whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value revealed earlier in the batch-major, slot-minor evaluation order of proof Section 7.2. Used only to lower-bound the success probability (Lemma 1 and bad events B1-B5). Output correctness and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: Fixed six-round prefix SHA3-256 restricted to 32-byte messages (4 variable input lanes, 21 constant lanes), iterated along chains from uniform 256-bit starts in 256 concurrent slots, over at most K0 + 256L < 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard van Oorschot-Wiener premise, accepted as plausible for the same step map in #28. Organizer-verified reduced-width (20-bit) runs of the same bit-sliced slot-DP walk on the real target support the mechanics; they are extrapolated qualitatively, not numerically, to the full 256-bit map. Published 5- and 6-round SHA3 cryptanalysis uses chosen differences, which a random walk does not produce.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is false as a literal statement about a fixed deterministic function. The experiments make no full-width probability estimate and their frequencies are descriptive only. The success bound 0.4107158 exceeds 0.39 by 0.0207, so a contact-probability shortfall of up to 0.0207 relative to H-RF still leaves the stated algorithm at or above 0.39; the 0.027 bits of time slack under 125.58 could raise K0 by about 0.06 bits if ever needed, but the claim is for the stated K0. Six-round SHA3-256 has known differential structure (a 6-bit near-collision is reported in ePrint 2026/2107); no evidence that the iterated map departs measurably from a random mapping was found in this survey.
